question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

It is 2036. Looking back, 5 landmark papers each settled this question in a way that surprised the field, because of how they approached it. For each paper, describe what it measured, analyzed, or did, as a concrete idea a research lab could pursue today. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Timed degron removal of AP-1 after priming
ideas.description: Tag endogenous FOS, FOSL1, and JUN family members with dTAG or auxin degrons and deplete them at defined intervals after a priming stimulus, then re-challenge the cells. Comparing loss of the remembered response when AP-1 is removed during writing versus long after it separates AP-1's establishment role from a continuous maintenance requirement.

ideas.title: Lineage-barcoded measurement of memory half-life
ideas.description: Combine clonal barcoding with sister-cell transcriptomics and ATAC profiling to quantify how many divisions AP-1 target programs and AP-1-bound accessible sites stay correlated within a clone. Running the same assay in AP-1-inhibited cells (A-FOS or compound knockouts) converts the qualitative memory claim into a measured decay timescale.

ideas.title: Hysteresis mapping with live AP-1 reporters
ideas.description: Image endogenous AP-1 activity together with upstream kinase reporters while slowly ramping a stimulus up and then back down over days. A memory mechanism should show a gap between the rising and falling dose-response curves, and the width of that gap gives the quantitative signature to compare across cell types and stimuli.

ideas.title: Synthetic AP-1 tethering as a sufficiency test
ideas.description: Use inducible dCas9 or optogenetic recruitment to deposit AP-1 subunits at defined loci for a brief window, then release them and track accessibility, histone marks, and re-inducibility for weeks. This asks whether AP-1 occupancy alone, with no upstream signaling, is sufficient to write a persistent state.

ideas.title: Mitotic bookmarking and daughter-cell inheritance
ideas.description: Profile AP-1 binding and chromatin accessibility in synchronized mitotic cells and in freshly divided daughter pairs to see whether AP-1-marked sites are retained through chromosome condensation. Pairing this with live imaging of reporter reactivation timing in daughters tests whether physical inheritance, rather than re-establishment from signaling, carries the memory.
